newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE mission still set for Albania trip Thursday.
newsitem.headline: OSCE mission still set for Albania trip Thursday.

text.p: The OSCE's special envoy to Albania, former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, said on Thursday he would try to reach Tirana by military plane later in the day, despite reports that the airport there was closed.

Vranitzky, who first visited Tirana last week as head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission, told a news conference he would try at all costs to reach the Albanian capital as planned in the hope of trying to hold all-party talks which would include the rebels.

"The next important step is to involve the rebels in the political process," said Vranitzky, who earlier presented his report on the current crisis in Albania to the OSCE's Vienna-based permanent council.

Albania, Europe's poorest nation, has plunged into anarchy as looting of arms depots by rebels spread across the country and an anti-government uprising, sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes, gathered pace.
Vranitzky said he had not yet received word on whether his 10-member delegation could hold talks with insurgents who have taken control of the south of the Balkan state.

"We have had no direct reaction from anyone on behalf of the insurgents, but the message from the prime minister (Bashkim Fino) is that we may be able to have contact and might be able to organise talks," Vranitzky said.
Police manning a roadblock at the entrance to Tirana airport told a Reuter correspondent the airport was closed but that Vranitzky was still expected to arrive in the afternoon.
Vranitzky said a nine-point programme proposed by President Sali Berisha largely corresponded with the OSCE's suggestions, but needed to be shown to the insurgents.
"We demand dialogue with all political forces in Albania, the restoration of order and of public confidence in the political leadership and a concrete improvement of the economic situation," he said.
The former chancellor stressed that cooperation between political and financial institutions in Europe was vital to help resolve the crisis, since the OSCE could not do the job single-handedly.

"The World Bank and International Monetary Fund are immediately prepared to talk to Albania, on two conditions: the restoration of public order and the clear commitment to democratic politics in Albania," he said.
However, the OSCE saw no need for NATO intervention at this stage, he noted.

Vranitzky said the OSCE was not in a position to ask for Berisha's resignation, as demanded by the rebels. "We will, however, insist that the Albanian politicians carry out their job properly," he said.
Vranitzky first presented his mission's report on Wednesday to Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen of Denmark, which currently holds the chairmanship of the 54-member state OSCE.
"Violence by any side could spark a civil conflict of unforeseen dimension, plunging the country in a state of war," the report said.
